title: 共生社会デザイン概論
subtitle: Introduction to Designs for a Co-existing Society
teachers:
DOBASHI Yoshito
授業科目の学習・教育目標
educationalGoal:
The goal of this course is for students to understand the concept and realities of a co-existing society and to act toward its realization. The course will primarily focus on persons with disabilities as a representative case.
Students will study the philosophy and systems of disability welfare. Through this course, students are expected to: understand the importance of respecting minorities, learn about human rights,reflect upon these themes, and be able to explain them clearly.
advice:
(Course Overview)
1)Introduction, 2)Target groups in a co-existing society
3)Basic knowledge about persons with disabilities(PWD)
4)History of PWD, 5)Laws and systems supporting PWD
6)Living environments of PWD, 7)Key actors in disability welfare
8)Social work, 9)Disability and Development, 10)Disability welfare by local government
11)Various co-existing societies (gender, LGBTQ, children)
12)Various co-existing societies (people in poverty, single-parent households, elderly persons living alone, urban and rural disparities, homelessness)
13)Various co-existing societies (Zainichi foreign residents, migrants, refugees, indigenous peoples)
14)Special lecture by an external guest speaker
15)Course reflection
(Advice for Students)
Pay attention to daily life, newspapers, and news to deepen interest in co-existing society issues.
A special lecture by external practitioners/persons concerned is scheduled (some changes may occur).
books:
1)Oliver Michael, Sapey Bob, Thomas Pam：Social work with disabled people (4th edition). Bloomsbury Publishing, (2012).
2)Schein Edgar H.：Helping: How to Offer, Give, and Receive Help. Berrett-Koehler, (2011).
3)Kallen Evelyn：Social inequality and social injustice: A human rights perspective. Palgrave Macmillan Basingstoke, UK, (2004).
requiredKnowledge:
No specific prior knowledge or skills are required.
However, students are expected to have an interest in current affairs and social issues in daily life. Some English-language materials may occasionally be used for reference purposes; however, it is sufficient if students can grasp the general atmosphere and meaning.

activityGoals.body: Acquire and be able to explain basic information about a co-existing society and persons with disabilities.
Understand issues concerning a co-existing society and persons with disabilities as issues affecting society.
Develop the ability to think and act without discrimination between majority and minority groups, and others.
Acquire the ability to gather knowledge and information and solve problems faced by international society.
Understand knowledge and structures concerning humans, society, and nature; from regional to global level.
Identify issues in local communities and society and develop plans to address diverse social challenges

achievementLevels.ideal:
Accurately understands knowledge of a co-existing society and can persuasively explain the needs of minorities.
Accurately understands knowledge concerning persons with disabilities and can logically explain both the necessity and limitations of disability welfare.
Demonstrates deep understanding of disability welfare issues that are current social concerns and can clearly articulate those issues.
Through understanding disability-related challenges, demonstrates deep understanding of the realities of a co-existing society and can explain them accurately.
Fully understands the ideal form of a co-existing society and can logically express personal views.
achievementLevels.standard:
Generally understands fundamental knowledge of a co-existing society and can explain the needs of minorities.
Generally understands basic knowledge about persons with disabilities and can explain the necessity and limitations of disability welfare.
Generally understands disability welfare issues that are current social concerns and can explain them.
Through understanding disability-related challenges, generally understands and can explain the realities of a co-existing society.
Generally understands the ideal form of a co-existing society and can express personal views.
